title: Replace the provisional control-room approval refusal channel with the landed vocabulary
description:
CONSUMER EDGE for task-5d8f11c86a3a41b4a8a420ef0d52a444. Clause 1 requires this task to exist.

THE PROVISIONAL MARKER THAT NAMES THIS WORK: apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts carries an approval refusal-reason channel EXPLICITLY MARKED PROVISIONAL pending the daemon's stable reason registry (spec section 13-D2). That registry now exists for the approval decision. Re-read the file before planning and confirm the marker is still there and still says that — task rail 6: a description's claims about disk are stale by default, in BOTH directions.

WHAT LANDED (commit 18f0964, published from the @moe/core root, verify by grep before naming symbols):
- APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES, 8 stable codes: APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED, APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH, APPROVAL_PRINCIPAL_MISSING, APPROVAL_PRINCIPAL_UNNAMED, APPROVAL_PRINCIPAL_NOT_HUMAN, APPROVAL_GRANT_MOMENT_INVALID, APPROVAL_POLICY_DELAY_INVALID, APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED.
- APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS, 2: HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE, APPROVAL_POLICY. The layer is what tells a reader WHICH refusal answered, and the UI should surface it — "refused" alone is what the contract exists to stop being the whole story.
- APPROVAL_POLICY_KINDS and the ApprovalPolicy union for rendering the policy in force.
- HumanAuthorityGate / HumanAuthorityGrant for rendering a gate and who satisfied it.

DEPENDENCY EDGE, verify all three before planning (project rail 7 — this repo has no tsconfig "paths" and no project references, so a deep relative import fails with TS6059): (a) apps/control-room/package.json declares @moe/core in "dependencies"; (b) pnpm-lock.yaml carries the importer entry; (c) a compiled probe inside apps/control-room importing from the BARE specifier "@moe/core" typechecks exit 0, probe deleted in the same command. If the edge is absent, the first plan step is the manifest edit plus workspace install, with both files declared as owned paths — never plan around the gap.

SCOPE: the control-room approval surface only. Render the policy in force, render a human authority gate and its grant, and map every refusal to its exact code AND layer. NOT IN SCOPE: the daemon wiring (task-5fcfdae58ec7419fbcba0000ef08d3b6), the orchestrator settings file, or changing the contract.

WORTH KNOWING: the gate's whole point is that no UI control can satisfy it. A "force approve" affordance is not a missing feature — do not add one. Satisfying a gate takes a named human principal through grantHumanAuthority; an agent, and a button that calls one, cannot.
definitionOfDone: The PROVISIONAL marker in apps/control-room/src/approvals/approval-gating.ts is gone, and its refusal channel now carries codes from the landed APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES rather than a local provisional set.

Every rendered refusal shows the stable code AND the refusing layer; a test asserts both literally for at least one gate-layer and one policy-layer refusal, never merely that the control was disabled.

The dependency edge from apps/control-room to @moe/core is verified three ways - manifest dependency, lockfile importer entry, and a bare-specifier probe that typechecks exit 0 and is deleted in the same command.
The surface offers no affordance that approves gated work; a test enumerates every approval control against a gated unit and asserts each is refused or absent, with a nonzero exact cardinality.
A mutation drill weakening the code-to-layer mapping turns a named test red on its code-and-layer assertion, restored byte-exact and verified by hash.

implementationPlan.description: Write the red tests first in `approval-gating.test.tsx`. Replace assertions for the provisional runtime-code/source channel with a literal eight-entry code@layer expectation exercised through the production `approvalReason` surface; assert the generated count equals `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES.length`, equals 8, and is nonzero. Add DOM assertions that a gate refusal visibly renders `APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED` plus `HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE`, and a policy refusal visibly renders `APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` plus `APPROVAL_POLICY` (not only disabled state/data attributes). Render both policy kinds, an unsatisfied gate, and a granted gate whose named HUMAN principal, gate/work binding, and grant moment are shown. Build a uniquely-qualified request for every `APPROVAL_DECISION_KINDS` member against one unsatisfied gate, assert the generated request/result cardinality is exact and nonzero, and assert every production resolver result is DISABLED or ABSENT with null commandId—never enabled. Preserve existing structural-guard coverage while updating it to assert the new stable code, canonical layer, and the separate local guard that answered.

Failures specifically showed the first landed code rejected by the provisional runtime registry, old EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT copy lacking layer, supplied authority ignored/enabled, no authority presentation in DOM, and local guards still emitting old runtime codes. Added literal 8-entry code@layer assertion with count==registry==8>0, visible gate/policy refusal assertions, both policy/grant render cases, exact nonzero all-decision control sweep, and structural guard code+layer+local-guard assertions. Test file remains 291 lines.

implementationPlan.description: Replace the provisional channel in `approval-gating.ts` with the landed @moe/core vocabulary. Import the runtime registries and `decideApprovalAuthority` from the bare package root plus the public policy/gate/grant/refusal types; remove `lookupRuntimeError`, RuntimeErrorCode/source validation, the PROVISIONAL comment, and the local runtime-code set. Define one frozen exhaustive `Record<ApprovalAuthorityCode, ApprovalAuthorityLayer>` with the six gate codes mapped to HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE and the two policy codes mapped to APPROVAL_POLICY; construct every `ApprovalReason` from that mapping so invented codes or wrong code/layer pairs are not representable. Carry `code`, `refusingLayer`, phrase, and the existing local `refusedBy` diagnostic separately on controls, and make unavailable copy include code and layer literally. Accept a supplied `{policy, gate}` authority context on approval requests, evaluate it once with `decideApprovalAuthority` before lifecycle/validity/hash checks, attach its policy/gate/result plus the record's existing truth class for presentation, and null commandId on refusal. Translate the existing stale lifecycle/validity/revision-binding client refusals to `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH@HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE` while retaining their precise phrases and local guard IDs. When no authority context is supplied, invent nothing and retain the pre-existing nextAllowedCommands-only behavior pending the separately scoped daemon wiring task. Keep the production file at or below 250 physical lines by deleting obsolete registry commentary and compacting helpers, not by weakening checks.
implementationPlan.note: Replaced the provisional contracts runtime-error channel with a frozen exhaustive 8-code canonical layer map and bare @moe/core decision/types. Resolver snapshots/evaluates one supplied authority context once before local guards, rejects malformed supplied context with APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH@HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE, never invents context when absent, nulls command IDs on refusals, and attaches frozen policy/gate/validated grant/result/truth presentation. All structural refusals retain precise phrases/local guard IDs while emitting the stable binding code/layer. Production file is 241 lines; PROVISIONAL/lookupRuntimeError/RuntimeErrorCode/grantHumanAuthority are absent. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` exited 0. Two focused Vitest retries were attempted, but the loaded shared host failed to start the sole worker within 60s (`Test Files no tests`, infrastructure timeout); no test pass was claimed, and the concentrated green run remains required in step 5.

implementationPlan.description: Update the canonical `DecisionControl` rendering in `approval-inbox.tsx`. For every disabled/refused control, expose the stable code and canonical layer as distinct data attributes and visible operator text while retaining the local guard identifier for diagnostics. When the resolver supplies authority presentation, render the policy kind (and explicit delay for PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN), gate id/work reference/satisfied state, and grant principal kind/id/moment through existing truth-preserving `FactRow` primitives using the record's supplied truth class; render no claims when the context was not supplied. A null grant is stated as unsatisfied, not treated as permission. Add no click handler, button, callback, or command that grants/overrides a gate; `onActivate` remains unreachable for refused controls. Keep ABSENT controls absent and preserve exact cr.fact/cr.chip prefix cardinality and unique IDs. Refactor/condense existing prose or helpers as needed so this production file remains at or below 250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note: DecisionControl now exposes data-reason-code, data-refusing-layer, and data-refused-by separately; visible disabled copy contains code@layer. Supplied authority context renders policy/delay, gate id/work/satisfied state, and only a validated grant's HUMAN principal/id/moment through FactList→FactRow with the record truth class. Fact IDs include each unique control test ID. Missing context yields zero authority facts; null/invalid grants display UNSATISFIED and no principal claim. Inline inbox choices pass optional supplied authority; no grant/force/override affordance or import exists and refused controls have no activation handler. approval-inbox.tsx is 231 lines. Control-room typecheck exited 0. Focused Vitest was retried with a single threads worker, but the shared host again timed out starting that worker at 60s (`Test Files no tests`); this is recorded as unverified, not a pass, and step 5 still requires a real nonzero test count.

Read output, not only exit status: the control-room, root, and daemon Vitest legs must each print a nonzero `Test Files`/test count and none may say `No projects matched`, `No test files found`, or `0 passed`. Compare repo-wide failing paths with the recorded pre-edit baseline; owned-package legs must be exit 0, and any foreign red must be reported verbatim with the path-attributed delta proving no new failure intersects these five owned paths.

implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review found and fixed two real fail-closed gaps: structurally forged code/layer pairs supplied through the reasons boundary were previously passed through, and repeated requests produced duplicate control/fact IDs. New production normalization degrades malformed pairs to APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH@HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE, ApprovalReason is a code-correlated discriminated union, and resolver-local Set deduplication preserves the first control without creating authority. Review also found repeated reads of hostile authority getters; snapshotRequest now reads gate/policy once. TDD red proved the first two failures (2 failed/21 passed) and the getter read twice; green is 23/23, full control-room 70 files/860 tests. No shared mutable state/concurrency race; all failure paths are pure/no side effects. Malformed/null/empty/non-human authority remains refused with exact codes and null commandId; supplied gate precedes policy/local guards; absent controls remain absent; no grantHumanAuthority/force/grant affordance exists. planningNotes.risks: Keep the local guard identifier (`refusedBy`) distinct from the landed authority layer (`refusingLayer`): the former explains which client integrity check ran, while the latter is the stable contract field the operator must see. Evaluate a supplied authority context before local lifecycle/validity/hash checks so an unconditional gate cannot leak an enabled command. Do not accept arbitrary code/layer cross-products; derive/validate the canonical layer from an exhaustive production mapping (first six codes gate layer, final two policy layer). Do not fabricate an authority context when the daemon has not supplied one; omission renders no policy/gate/grant claims and preserves nextAllowedCommands as the only existing command authority. Reuse the record's supplied truth class when rendering authority facts, never upgrade it. Avoid duplicate cr.fact/cr.chip prefix IDs when multiple controls render. No production import or call of grantHumanAuthority and no grant/force button.
